newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court limits Council's right to derogate from VAT directive.
newsitem.headline: Court limits Council's right to derogate from VAT directive.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the Council of the European Union cannot introduce special measures to Community tax rules for associated persons under the VAT directive except to prevent tax avoidance.

The court found the Council's authority under article 27(1) of the directive to enact derogating measures must be aimed at preventing tax evasion or avoidance. "The authorization cannot extend beyond that purpose," the court said.

"An authorization by the Council to introduce a special measure for derogation from the Sixth VAT directive, whereby ...in the case of supplies for consideration made between associated persons, the cost to the taxable person...is to be used as the minimum basis of assessment, is not covered by article 27 of the directive where the agreed consideration represents the market rate but is less than the minimum basis of assessment," the court said.
"Sixth VAT directive - Personal relationship between the supplier and the recipient of the supply"

on the interpretation of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC on the harmonization of laws relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

An authorization by the Council to introduce a special measure for derogation from the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC on the harmonization of laws relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment) whereby, in the case of supplies for consideration made between associated persons the cost to the taxable person within the meaning of article 11(A)(1)(c) of the Sixth directive is to be used as the minimum basis of assessment is not covered by article 27 of the directive where the agreed consideration represents the market rate but is less than the minimum basis of assessment.
